title: SQL trace rollup routing in raw_range_points: read non-grouped raw gaps before the final rollup_read_is_current recheck, and fall back to one full raw query if it fails
answers: Trace metric counts look inconsistent or double-counted after a rollup rebuild on MSSQL
Why does a trace metric query fall back to a full raw scan when a rollup day was invalidated?
Where is the rollup validity check ordered relative to the raw-gap query in trace metrics?
Why does the grouped (sql_grouped_merge) trace metric path skip this reordering?
body:
Path: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:raw_range_points serves trace metric queries (trace count and other trace metric views, bucketed or unbucketed, with max_results) from the SQL trace rollup when it is enabled. It merges the selected rollup contribution (served.data_points) with raw trace rows for the gap ranges (served.raw_ranges).
Rule: For non-SQL-grouped plans, read the raw gaps (raw_range_points over served.raw_ranges with raw_aggregations_for_plan) before calling rollup_read_is_current(session, plan, served.served_day_starts_ms). Only then decide: if the check passes, merge rollup and raw; if it fails, discard the mixed result and run one authoritative full-range raw query. Do not move the validity check back above the raw-gap read.
Symptom: On MSSQL under REPEATABLE READ, a rebuild could be queued after the validity check but before the raw-gap read. Stale rollup data was then merged with newer raw data, so the returned trace metric values did not match the traces that existed.
Constraints: Applies to the served-rollup branch only. The SQL-grouped path is unchanged because it reads rollup and raw-gap contributions in one SQL query. Covered by test_raw_gap_is_read_before_final_invalidation_check, which asserts the event order raw gap, then validity check, then full raw fallback by patching query_metrics and rollup_read_is_current.
applies: SQL trace rollup read routing in the SQLAlchemy tracking store; applies to any change to the order of raw-gap reads, validity checks, or fallback in raw_range_points.
says: Trace metric charts show inconsistent or duplicate counts after recent data updates.
The trace count graph displays double-counted numbers instead of matching existing traces.
Trace metric views should display accurate historical totals without mixing stale rollup data.
Trace metrics query results on SQL databases mismatch actual trace records during rollup recalculation.
search: In mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:raw_range_points, non-grouped SQL trace rollup queries must read raw gap ranges before calling rollup_read_is_current, falling back to a full raw query if the check fails. If rollup_read_is_current passes, merge the rollup contribution (served.data_points) and raw gaps; if it fails, discard the mixed result and run one authoritative full-range raw query. This prevents merging stale rollup data with newer raw data on MSSQL under REPEATABLE READ when a rebuild is queued between the check and gap read. The rule applies only to the served-rollup branch in raw_range_points and leaves the grouped sql_grouped_merge path unchanged.
